correctness.rationale: For every i in nonempty I, if f({i}) contains two target atoms a,b, the back property supplies source sets meeting {i} with disjoint singleton images; they meet each other, contradicting forth. Hence f({i})={pi(i)}. Forth yields pi[S] subset f(S), back to each target singleton yields the reverse inclusion. Back to J forces pi onto. Every surjective pi induces back via T=pi^{-1}(Y). The proof covers arbitrary nonempty (possibly infinite) carriers; categorical composition, n!S(m,n) finite count and automorphism group then follow. Direct independent enumeration of all maps for (1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(3,1),(3,2) matched (1,0,1,2,0,1,6), and packaged checker.py source uses the literal forth/back tests. This checks finite cases only, not infinite via computation.
